issuer: the Registrar of Motor Vehicles of the Northern Territory (the Motor Vehicle Registry)
note: Read 2026-10-30 on the Northern Territory's legislation site. The Motor Vehicles Act 1949: a learner licence from 16 (s 9(4)), held at least 6 months before a licence is granted (s 10(1A)); a licence granted to someone who hasn't held one is provisional for 2 years if they are under 25 (s 10A): a full licence is had from 18 years 6 months, kept as 19 (a whole-year age, rounded up). The Motor Vehicles Regulations 1977 (in force at 18 November 2025), reg 8, make the prescribed period of a licence 10 years (s 104 lets the applicant ask for a shorter one, at least 12 months), held as the term until 2026-10-30. The Motor Vehicles (Fees and Charges) Regulations 2008 (in force at 1 July 2026) price the issue or renewal of a driver licence by its term (Schedule 1, Part 2, item 1): 27 revenue units for 12 months, 41 for 2 years, 82 for 5 and 141 for 10, 16.4 for each year of a licence of more than 2 but less than 5 years and 14.1 for each year of one of more than 5 but less than 10. Until 2026-10-30 the file held the 10-year licence with its fee null: the revenue unit's dollar value for 2026-27, set under the Revenue Units Act 2009 and published by the Treasury, wasn't read (its page refused the request behind a Cloudflare check). From 2026-10-30 it holds the ten whole-year terms an applicant may ask for under s 104(1), one to ten years, each in revenue units worth the unit's value on the day paid (the game holds the Territory's revenue unit, NTRU, and rounds a fee down to the dollar as the Revenue Units Act does): 1 year 27, 2 years 41, 3 and 4 years 16.4 for each year, 5 years 82, 6 to 9 years 14.1 for each year, 10 years 141. A term of months beyond whole years, which s 104(1) allows, and the period the Registrar sets under s 104(2)(b)(ii) (item 1(i)) aren't held. NT.GOV.AU's licence pages refused the same way. The Territory's evidence of age card isn't held.
